hero.headline: Build with AI. Ship for real.
hero.sub: Spec-driven × AI agents × full-stack delivery. I don't just use AI to write code — I manage how AI works, and I build tools for it.

about.heading: About
about.short: Japanese Literature major turned AI-Native Software Engineer (JLPT N1). I ship enterprise systems (Text-to-SQL, an SRE triage agent, a job scheduler), ML models and cloud infrastructure with a spec-driven, AI-agent workflow, and launch my own products with the same workflow in days; I write Claude Skills, built an MCP Gateway, and teach the workflow internally. In the AI era an engineer's value is judgment and process design, not typing speed.

acts.title: Act 1: An unusual start
acts.body: Japanese Literature degree, JLPT N1. My career began with language; a six-month AI/cloud bootcamp moved me into engineering. I built AI applications at a startup (content-to-video, LINE avatars and voice cloning) and now work as a Senior Systems Analyst at a retail group's IT subsidiary, spanning data engineering, DevOps and cloud architecture.

acts.title: Act 2: AI changed how I work
acts.body: Over the past year I moved my workflow to spec-driven development with AI agents: brainstorm → design spec → implementation plan → TDD, where AI executes and I review and decide. Real projects grew it into my own version — design phases produce only documents, and subagents implement only after decisions are final; a self-made dispatch skill routes each task to the cheapest model that is good enough; one shared AGENTS.md drives two agents; an automated AI code-review loop. With it I independently delivered an enterprise allocation platform (2.5 months), a CDP's AI service and job scheduler (88 commits and 1,190 unit tests in one day), took Text-to-SQL from PoC to a production service, and built a company MCP Gateway in 3 days. After hours, same workflow: a ramen map live on day one, a Japanese typing trainer with 470 tests in 3 working days. Every number is in the git history.

acts.title: Act 3: From user to builder
acts.body: I don't just use AI tools — I package team domain knowledge as Claude Skills with evals, built the gateway that lets every AI tool in the company reach internal APIs safely, wrote a Claude Code mod that shows context usage and cost in real time, and draw boundaries for AI agents: proposal-only changes gated by automated tests, zero shell and zero cloud permissions, never writing to third-party platforms on a user's behalf. I also learned to reject upgrades with data: a 65-case eval showed the bottleneck was the rules, not the model, so I built human-precedent override instead and triage accuracy went from 12% to 80%. Next: build something that actually matters.

items.name: Career Agent
items.tagline: AI job-search assistant: upload résumé → AI diagnosis → auto-crawl listings → fit ranking → tailored cover letters → application board
items.story: Built so others could solve their own problem with a tool. The launch post on Threads passed 10K views and it has real users. It later grew a local edition: reads your logged-in job-site data and runs a tool-use chat agent as a "job-search commander" — but the agent never applies on your behalf.

items.name: SRE-agent
items.tagline: Azure Data Factory failure triage: read-only against ADF, detects failures every 5 minutes → de-duplicates into incidents → rules first, LLM as fallback → a Teams card tells the on-call engineer the conclusion, what to do now and what to check first
items.story: Rejected a model upgrade with data: on 65 eval cases Opus looked far ahead, but with duplicates removed it tied with gpt-mini — the bottleneck was the actions the rules suggested, not the model. So I built human-precedent override instead. The learning agent is proposal-only: a human clicks apply, pytest reverts failures, passing changes commit; zero shell, zero Azure permissions. Designed and built solo in about five weeks.

items.name: Text-to-SQL
items.tagline: Natural-language queries over 920M transaction rows: understand → code-side guards → option-based clarification → generate SQL → validation and an EXPLAIN gate → code computes statistics, the LLM only interprets
items.story: From PoC to a production service: sqlglot dialect packs for both T-SQL and PostgreSQL, a semantic model where every fact carries confidence and evidence, 10 ADRs. Guard rule: any condition that cannot become SQL is asked back, never silently dropped. Once other systems asked to onboard, the positioning became "the execution engine plus a 13-step onboarding process is the product".

items.name: menmap (麵咩撲)
items.tagline: Taipei ramen map: daily Google Maps harvesting → open-now / metro / style filters → a "where today" dice → ramen diary and friends
items.story: Fourteen minutes from pricing Google Places API to dropping it: the scraper runs at home and the cloud only reads. Tests showed datacenter IPs get degraded, stripped-down pages, so the collector stays home. LLM classification of 491 shops cost US$2.5. Worker-rendered SEO pages, self-written Google OAuth, $0 a month.

items.name: pachipachi (ぱちぱち)
items.tagline: Japanese typing trainer: romaji input judged key by key into kana, from kana charts to N1 vocabulary, timed leaderboards, and your own lyrics synced to YouTube
items.story: Seven worktree subagents built it in parallel and merged the same day. The server recomputes every score from the client's key log and applies six anticheat rules — it never trusts client numbers. Lyrics copyright was researched (JASRAC, Taiwan copyright law) before design: shared timelines store only hashes, notice-and-takedown, three strikes.

items.name: MCP Gateway
items.tagline: Wraps internal enterprise APIs as MCP tools so any AI coding agent reaches them safely through one entry point
items.story: Design focus: per-client auth, SSRF protection, encrypted upstream credentials, audit logs with sensitive-parameter masking — both input and output are recorded. Tool catalog lives in a DB; approved tools go live without code changes or restarts. One admin page generates connection configs for eight AI clients.

items.name: Enterprise delivery
items.tagline: Retail allocation platform, CDP batch evolution and job scheduler, performance root-causing, demand-forecasting ML, Azure IaC
items.story: Delivered solo with AI collaboration at a retail group's IT subsidiary: a 2.5-month allocation platform (FastAPI + React 19); ADF polling replaced by a queue, then by a single-table scheduler, with the production cutover led by me; three measurement-first performance root-causes with zero builder changes; LightGBM/CatBoost allocation models; Bicep IaC reconciled with portal drift.

items.name: Suancui (酸脆)
items.tagline: Threads AI roast generator: enter a handle → four roast styles as share cards → share to unlock hidden styles
items.story: Product thinking and a lesson in failure: Threads' anti-scraping returned 200 with gutted content, so the AI fabricated personalities. "Never fabricate" became a product rule. It spread less than Career Agent — tools that solve real problems travel further than entertainment.
